title: Continuous integral fibre reconstruction and normalized rational realization
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Assume also that its underlying topological space is Noetherian and that $X$ is quasi-separated. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and put $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar x)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $X$, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$, where the terms are constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put $R_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Identify these with the continuous-function integral and rational coefficient sheaves using [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence] and localization at $\ell$ or $\varpi$. Let $J_X$ be any fully faithful $E$-linear representation-realization functor with lisse values and the simultaneous integral normalizations of [lem-sfb-etale-local-monodromy-realization, def-sfb-monodromy-realization-data]. Its source consists of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces with jointly continuous $\Pi$-action for their product $\ell$-adic topology, with equivariant linear maps.

Let $M$ be a lisse $B_X$-module, meaning a sheaf module pro-etale locally finite free, with rank zero allowed [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $(F_n)_{n\geq1}$ be its normalized tower of finite locally free etale $A/\varpi^n$-module sheaves under [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], so $M\cong\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*F_n$, with $\nu_X^*$ the comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Put $\Lambda_n=(F_n)_{\bar x}$, with its finite discrete continuous $\Pi$-action from [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1). Then the fibre transitions are equivariant and induce $\Lambda_{n+1}/\varpi^n\Lambda_{n+1}\cong\Lambda_n$. The module $\Lambda=\varprojlim_n\Lambda_n$ is finite free over $A$, its projections induce equivariant isomorphisms $\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda\cong\Lambda_n$, and its inverse-limit topology equals its $\varpi$-adic topology. The coordinatewise action $\Pi\times\Lambda\to\Lambda$ is jointly continuous.

Set $V=E\otimes_A\Lambda$. Then $V$ is finite dimensional and its induced action is jointly continuous for the product $\ell$-adic topology. The canonical map $\Lambda\to V$ is injective and exhibits $\Lambda$ as a stable finite free lattice. The finite-level correspondence identifies $F_n$ with the local system associated to $\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda$, compatibly with all quotient transitions. For the specified $J_X$ and its integral normalization there is consequently an isomorphism $J_X(V)\cong M[1/\varpi]$ of lisse $R_X$-modules. No normality hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the normalized etale tower supplied by lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison. Its terms are finite locally free over the finite rings $A/\varpi^n$, so their stalks $\Lambda_n$ are finite free over these rings (evaluate an etale local trivialization at $\bar x$). Apply cor-galois-lisse-representations(1) to each finite level. It gives the continuous discrete actions and makes every transition equivariant. Its compatibility with finite-ring scalar extension carries the given isomorphism $F_{n+1}\otimes_{A/\varpi^{n+1}}A/\varpi^n\cong F_n$ to $\Lambda_{n+1}/\varpi^n\Lambda_{n+1}\cong\Lambda_n$, with the actual transition as quotient map. In Lean use the existing linear fibre path family to define each representation and transport its evaluation formula to the actual stalk; continuity follows from the finite correspondence topology.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), p. 59, and the integral finite-monodromy reduction in Corollary 6.8.5, p. 60

proof.text: The tower in Step 1 satisfies part (1) of lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules, with $\mathcal O_E=A$ and $\varpi_E=\varpi$. Hence $\Lambda=\varprojlim_n\Lambda_n$ is finitely generated over $A$, the projections give $\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda\cong\Lambda_n$, and the inverse-limit topology is the $\varpi$-adic topology. On compatible tuples define $g(x_n)_n=(gx_n)_n$. Equivariance of the transitions makes this a well-defined $A$-linear group action. Every projection is equivariant by this formula, so its induced quotient isomorphism is equivariant too.

source.place: Tag 09B8 (lemma-limit-complete) and Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring), as assembled in lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules(1)

proof.text: To prove torsion-freeness, suppose $\varpi x=0$ in $\Lambda$. For each $n\geq1$, the coordinate $x_{n+1}$ is killed by $\varpi$ in a free $A/\varpi^{n+1}$-module. In each free coordinate, $\varpi a\in\varpi^{n+1}A$ implies $a\in\varpi^nA$, since $A$ is a domain and $\varpi\ne0$. Thus $x_{n+1}\in\varpi^n\Lambda_{n+1}$, whose image in $\Lambda_n$ is zero by Step 1. All $x_n$ vanish, hence $x=0$. Repeatedly applying this implication shows $\varpi^s x=0\Rightarrow x=0$ for every $s\geq0$. By lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr, $A$ is a DVR and every nonzero $a\in A$ is $u\varpi^s$ with $u$ a unit and $s\geq0$. Therefore $\Lambda$ is torsion-free. Apply lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free to the finitely generated module of Step 2: $\Lambda$ is finite free, including the zero module.

source.place: Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (3); the torsion-freeness calculation is written out here

proof.text: For each $n$, the $n$-th coordinate of the action is $(g,x)\mapsto g p_n(x)$, the composite of $\operatorname{id}\times p_n:\Pi\times\Lambda\to\Pi\times\Lambda_n$ and the continuous finite-level action supplied by cor-galois-lisse-representations(1). Thus every coordinate map is continuous. The topology of the inverse limit is the subspace topology of the product of the discrete $\Lambda_n$, so a map with values in that limit is continuous exactly when all its coordinates are continuous: inverse images of its basic open sets are finite intersections of coordinate inverse images. This proves joint continuity, not merely continuity for each fixed $g$. By Step 2 the same assertion holds for the $\varpi$-adic topology.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-integral-representation-rationalization] to the finite free integral limit representation. Its basis-coordinate argument proves injectivity of the tensor unit, finite dimensionality, the invariant lattice and joint rational continuity.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5, p. 60: explicit scalar-extension topology check for the integral-monodromy reduction

proof.text: Let $\mathcal L_n$ be the finite local system associated to $\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda$. Step 2 identifies this representation equivariantly with $\Lambda_n$. By full faithfulness and essential surjectivity of cor-galois-lisse-representations(1), the specified fibre identification lifts to an isomorphism $\mathcal L_n\cong F_n$. For successive transitions both composites in the required square have the same map on fibres, namely the projection of a compatible tuple to level $n$. Faithfulness therefore makes the square commute. This proves the identification of the entire inverse diagram, including all transitions, rather than just an isomorphism at each level. Use [lem-a1-finite-fibre-linear-lifting] for the unique levelwise linear lift; faithfulness identifies all transition squares. The faithful stalk and equality-detection helpers are reused from Sheaf.Paper.LatticeNormalizationRationalExact, where their unchanged proofs transport the given finite correspondence; its rational-exactness theorem is not used.

proof.text: The entire normalized etale diagram is now identified. Apply [lem-a1-completed-normalization-recovery] to recover the specified J(V) as actual scalar extension of M. This uses both limit cones, continuous integral scalar compatibility and uniqueness of coefficient extension; no replacement realization or normality is used.

S3 torsion-freeness is checked correctly through ann(ϖ) = ϖ^n in a free A/ϖ^{n+1}-module plus the dvr(2),(5) factorization; it does not claim that a limit of torsion-free modules is torsion-free; then the DVR freeness leaf. S4 coordinatewise continuity is elementary. S5 the topologies agree via ϖ^nA^d balls (discrete value group), and the ϖ^{-r}Λ open cover gives joint continuity on Π×V; d=0 is fine. S6 full faithfulness lifts the fibre identification, and faithfulness gives the commuting transition squares, so the whole diagram is identified. S7 uses the stipulated J_X normalization from lem-sfb-etale-local/def-sfb on the lattice Λ (X connected, qcqs, topologically Noetherian), reindexed; lem-per gives M ≅ lim ν^*F_n; ℓ = uϖ^e with e > 0, so inverting ℓ or ϖ gives the same localization; the A_X/E_X vs B_X/R_X coefficients are matched by lem-sfb-integral exactly as the statement stipulates. No replacement functor, no normality, no SGA. No cycle.
